findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the deletion-safety rationale in the Deletions section: `src/rebar/graph/__init__.py:28`'s `__all__` exports 12+ symbols from four submodules — the safety argument should say 'none of the four deleted symbols appear in `__all__`' rather than claiming only two symbols are re-exported.
evidence: src/rebar/graph/__init__.py lines 28-41 exports: build_dep_graph, check_cycle_at_level, check_would_create_cycle, resolve_hierarchy_link, compute_archive_eligible, CyclicDependencyError, add_dependency, reduce_ticket, _is_active_link, _find_direct_blockers, _compute_dep_graph — 11 named symbols plus submodule names

findings.finding: The plan's deletion-safety argument (Deletions section) states '`__all__` (`src/rebar/graph/__init__.py:28`) re-exports only `resolve_hierarchy_link` and `compute_archive_eligible` from this module' — but the actual `__all__` exports 12+ symbols from four submodules (`CyclicDependencyError`, `add_dependency`, `_is_active_link`, `build_dep_graph`, `check_cycle_at_level`, `check_would_create_cycle`, etc.). A reviewer auditing the deletion-safety argument against the source will find the stated rationale factually wrong, undermining trust in the argument even though the underlying conclusion (the four tier symbols aren't in `__all__`) is correct.
findings.location: Deletions section — 'The package `__all__` (`src/rebar/graph/__init__.py:28`) re-exports only `resolve_hierarchy_link` and `compute_archive_eligible` from this module'
scenarios: A reviewer cross-checking the deletion-safety argument against __init__.py finds a discrepancy and must independently re-verify the conclusion, eroding confidence in the plan's accuracy claims.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'The package `__all__` re-exports only `resolve_hierarchy_link` and `compute_archive_eligible` from this module' with 'None of the four deleted symbols appear in `src/rebar/graph/__init__.py`'s `__all__`, so removing them cannot break any external import of the `rebar.graph` package surface.'

findings.finding: AC 13 proves that all five doc files describe the structural rule by requiring `grep -rln "nearest common ancestor"` to list all five paths, but the plan never mandates the exact phrase 'nearest common ancestor' in any of those files. The Scope section says only to 'restate [the tier rule] structurally' and 'describe the structural rule'. An implementation that uses equivalent but different wording (e.g. 'shared parent hierarchy', 'parent-based escalation') would satisfy the intent but cause the grep to return fewer than five paths, making AC 13 fail even though the docs are correctly updated — a taxonomy-item-4 fixture invalidity.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC 13: `grep -rln "nearest common ancestor" src/rebar/_cli/help/link.txt docs/ticket-model.md docs/cli-reference.md docs/user-guide.md docs/event-schema.md`
scenarios: An implementer accurately rewrites all five docs to describe NCA-based escalation using 'shared parent' or 'parent-level comparability' language; the grep returns 0 or <5 paths; AC 13 fails even though docs are correct.
Conversely, a search-and-replace that adds 'nearest common ancestor' to one sentence but leaves tier-language elsewhere passes the grep but doesn't satisfy AC 12.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Scope section: 'Each of the five files MUST include the phrase "nearest common ancestor" in its updated promotion description.' Then AC 13's grep is a valid fixture.

findings.finding: The plan changes the escalation semantics for cousin blocking links (a behavioral breaking change), and the store is durable — any edges written under the new semantics cannot be automatically un-done if the code is later rolled back. The plan addresses forward repair via sibling ticket 9ad7-d5a2-a664-4827 but provides no back-out procedure: if the new resolver is deployed and found to produce incorrect results, reverting the code leaves a mixed-state store (some edges written under old type-tier semantics, some under new structural semantics) with no described recovery path.
findings.location: Out of scope (deferred, not dropped) section; Approach — 'Cousins now escalate — an intended behaviour change'
scenarios: New semantics deployed; a production bug is discovered in the NCA algorithm; code is reverted to type-tier semantics; store now contains structurally-escalated edges that the reverted resolver no longer understands consistently.
